beats.text: You break a fifty. And somehow it's gone by Friday.
In one experiment, people got five dollars. Either as one bill, or as five ones or coins.
Those with small change spent more. The single bill mostly stayed in the pocket.
It's called the denomination effect. A big bill feels too whole to break.
So want to save? Keep it in one piece.

sources: Raghubir & Srivastava (2009). The denomination effect. Journal of Consumer Research 36(4). Gas-station experiment in Omaha: $5 as one bill vs five $1 bills or coins; small denominations spent more, the single bill mostly kept. Via NPR.
